instrument: ERCOT Nodal Protocols Section 3.14.1.1 (Notification of Suspension of Operations)
trigger_event: planned cessation/suspension of a Generation Resource for a period greater than 180 days (retirement or indefinite mothball); does not apply to a Forced Outage
source_doc: ERCOT Nodal Protocols, Section 3: Management Activities for the ERCOT System
notes: PRIMARY, verbatim: 'a Resource Entity must notify ERCOT in writing no less than 150 days prior to the date on which the Resource Entity intends to cease or suspend operation of a Generation Resource for a period of greater than 180 days.' Filed as a Notice of Suspension of Operations (NSO), Section 22 Attachment E (Parts I and II at filing; Part III due at filing or within 10 days of ERCOT's performance-deficiency determination).

source_doc: ERCOT Nodal Protocols, Section 3: Management Activities for the ERCOT System

instrument: ERCOT Nodal Protocols Section 3.14.1.2 (ERCOT Evaluation Process)
trigger_event: extension/backstop: deadline for ERCOT to clear the unit to retire or obtain ERCOT Board approval of an RMR/MRA Agreement, after which the Resource Entity may file a PUCT complaint (non-seasonal-mothball case; 90 days for the seasonal-mothball case)
source_doc: ERCOT Nodal Protocols, Section 3: Management Activities for the ERCOT System
notes: PRIMARY. ERCOT's analogue to an 'extended notice if RMR/reliability study triggered': ERCOT must complete its reliability analysis within 60 days of NSO receipt (3.14.1.2(5)); if, after 150 days following ERCOT's receipt of NSO Parts I and II (90 days for a seasonal-mothball NSO), ERCOT has neither notified the Resource Entity that continued operation is unneeded nor obtained ERCOT Board approval of an RMR/MRA Agreement, the Resource Entity may file a complaint with the PUCT under P.U.C. Subst. R. 25.502(e)(1). Separately, if a reliability issue is found, ERCOT issues an MRA Request for Proposal within 10 days and both parties begin RMR-Agreement negotiations within 11 days of the determination (3.14.1.2(6)-(7)).

instrument: PJM Manual 14D: Generator Operational Requirements, Section 9.1.1 (Generator Deactivation Notice)
trigger_event: planned deactivation/retirement -- minimum lead time under the current quarterly filing-and-processing cadence
source_doc: PJM Manual 14D: Generator Operational Requirements, Revision 70
notes: PRIMARY, current, directly rendered from the 230-page manual PDF. Materially different mechanism from the informal 90-day figure above. Verbatim rule: the desired Deactivation Date 'may be no earlier than' (a) July 1 of the current year if PJM receives notice Jan1-Mar31; (b) Oct 1 if received Apr1-Jun30; (c) Jan 1 of the following year if received Jul1-Sep30; (d) Apr 1 of the following year if received Oct1-Dec31. This lands the earliest allowed deactivation in the *second* subsequent quarter-start after the filing quarter -- a MINIMUM lead of roughly 3 months (if filed on the last day of a quarter) up to roughly 6 months (if filed on the first day). PJM's own Generation Deactivation Fact Sheet (dated 2026-04-20, separately retrieved) paraphrases this as 'notify PJM within the quarter that is at least two quarters before the proposed deactivation date.' 6 months is recorded here as that fact sheet's own stated floor ('at least two quarters'); treat this as a description of a quarterly cycle, not a single fixed day-count -- see the README for the full mechanics. DISCREPANCY FLAG: Manual 14D's own Revision History (document page 196) reads 'Revision 69 (12/17/2025): Section 9.1 ... Updated Section 9.1 to reflect a 12 month deactivation notification period,' but the Revision-70 body text in force as of the same effective date shows the quarterly-cadence rule above for ordinary units, NOT a flat 12-month notice. Recorded exactly as found; not resolved this session.

instrument: PJM Manual 14D: Generator Operational Requirements, Section 9.1.3 (Analysis Results)
trigger_event: extension: reliability issue identified in PJM's deactivation analysis -- deadline for PJM to publish the full transmission-upgrade requirements needed before the unit may deactivate
source_doc: PJM Manual 14D: Generator Operational Requirements, Revision 70
notes: PRIMARY. This is PJM's RMR-adjacent extension timeline -- the closest analogue to the repo comment's 'RMR study' extension. Full sequence once a reliability issue is identified: within 30 days of PJM's notice, the Generation Owner must state its intent regarding continued operation (incl. investment-cost/outage-time estimate if continuing); within 45 days PJM issues a revised transmission-upgrade completion estimate; within 60 days PJM publishes full upgrade-requirement details on its website. PJM has no authority to compel continued operation; a willing owner then negotiates compensation under OATT Part V Section 114 (Deactivation Avoidable Cost Rate/Credit) or files a cost-of-service rate under Section 119 (per Monitoring Analytics IMM memo to DESTF, 2023-10-12).

instrument: PJM OATT Attachment DD, Section 6.6(g) (RPM must-offer exception for a documented retirement plan)
trigger_event: notice required to avoid the RPM (capacity-auction) must-offer obligation on a unit with a documented plan to retire -- a capacity-market-participation carve-out, distinct from the physical Part V deactivation notice itself
source_doc: Monitoring Analytics (PJM's Independent Market Monitor), "IMM State of the Market Report discussion of Part V (RMR) issues," memo to the Deactivation Enhancements Senior Task Force, 2023-10-12
notes: Quasi-primary (PJM's own market monitor, citing the tariff section number directly), not independently rendered from agreements.pjm.com itself (same SPA-rendering block as the Section 113.1 row). Quoted: 'In order to avoid submitting an offer for a unit in the next three-year forward RPM base residual auction, an owner must show a documented plan in place to retire the resource ... including a notice of deactivation filed with PJM, 120 days prior to such auction.' Included because it is frequently conflated with the Section 113.1 deactivation notice in secondary commentary but is a separate must-offer-exception mechanism.

source_doc: FERC, Order Accepting Tariff Revisions re Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc., Docket No. ER23-630-000 (order dated 2023-02-10)
notes: Same 403-access caveat as the row above -- NOT independently rendered from MISO's own tariff PDF; recorded from consistent secondary corroboration only. FERC accepted MISO's proposal extending the Attachment Y suspension/retirement notice lead time 'from 26 weeks to four full quarterly study periods' (multiple WebSearch syntheses render this equivalently as roughly a year; one RTO Insider paraphrase states 'MISO generation owners must now give a year's advance notice ... before they can retire or suspend resources'). MISO's quarterly study-cycle windows reportedly begin March 1 / June 1 / September 1 / December 1, i.e. a request must be submitted at least four such quarters before the suspension start date. Recorded as 12 months / 'four quarters' per that corroboration. This is NOT the same parameter as the separate 3-year maximum-suspension-duration cap established by Docket No. ER18-1636 (order dated 2018-09-28, 'replace its retirement notification process with a more general three-year generation suspension period') -- see the README for that distinct figure.
